title: Tail amplification microprobe notes (scratch)
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad to capture an odd tail amplification effect observed when mixing short-chat (S) and long-context (L) requests in a single endpoint under moderate QPS. Trying to distill reproducible probe that isolates where the amplification appears (scheduler / batcher / device memory churn).

Hypothesis:
1) Head-of-line-ish: long-context requests cause KV-cache growth + kernel switching that increases variance for subsequent short requests (observable as amplified p99).
2) Batcher interaction: adaptive batcher holds short requests waiting for fill while long requests occupy GPU and push tail out.
3) Memory eviction / preemption: background GC or CUDA context flushes on long traces cause jitter spikes.

Testbed (minimal reproducible):
- Model: redwood-v1-8k (quantized int8 build) on a single A10G VM image.
- Runtime: local staging runtime from main (PR 1298 branch), continuous batching enabled, adaptive batch timeout = 12ms.
- Clients: two synthetic generators: S-gen (avg tokens out 12, latency budget 120ms), L-gen (avg tokens out 650, streaming disabled).
- Mix: baseline runs with pure S@200QPS, then S@200 + L@10, then S@200 + L@20. Each run: 10m warmup + 20m measurement.
- Tracing: token-level timestamps, KV cache size metric, batch size histogram, CUDA mem high-water mark sampled per-second.

Key knobs tried so far (notes):
- adaptive batch timeout: 12ms (default), 6ms, 25ms
- continuous batching: on/off
- prefetch KV cache keepalive: 30s/2m/inf
- priority lanes: enabled (short requests high-priority) vs disabled

Selected raw observations (aggregated):
Run A: pure-S @200QPS (control)
- p50 18ms, p95 42ms, p99 78ms
- batch size mode: 3
- CUDA mem HWM stable at 6.1GB

Run B: S200 + L10 (mixed)
- S requests p50 22ms (+4), p95 65ms (+23), p99 220ms (+142) 
- Occasional p99 spikes to 1.1s (3 samples) correlated with L-gen request start times
- batch size mode: S requests experienced higher variance in batch size (2-6)
- KV cache size: jumps during L requests (expected), spikes align with tail events

Run C: S200 + L20 (heavier)
- S p50 26ms, p95 84ms, p99 380ms (frequent 200-600ms tails)
- CUDA mem HWM climbed to 7.6GB during L bursts, followed by small pauses in scheduling (~50-120ms)

Quick ascii timeline (typical tail event):
T0: L request is dispatched (GPU kernel switch)
T0+10ms: batcher tries to coalesce S requests, but GPU busy -> queuing
T0+40ms: L continues, KV writes, small mem bump -> scheduler yields
T0+60-160ms: queued S requests start executing in small batches (latency realized as tail)

Short experiment matrix (what changed vs effect):
- Adaptive timeout -> lower (6ms): reduces p99 for S by ~20% in mixed runs but increases overall batch churn (more small batches).
- Continuous batching off: reduces tail magnitude but increases median by ~8-12ms (tradeoff).
- Priority lanes on (force S to preempt): eliminated >50% of p99 spikes but introduced rare starvation for L (observed L completion +150-300ms slower when preempted).
- KV keepalive inf: reduced mem churn but had diminishing returns; tail still present but rarer.

Preliminary interpretation:
- Main contributor seems to be scheduling interference when L triggers kernel/config changes and memory allocations (quantized model working sets + streaming). While GPU is servicing a long request, short requests are held and then executed in uneven small batches -> tail amplification.
- Two effective mitigations: 1) stricter prioritization for S (fast-path lane), 2) tune adaptive batch timeout lower to avoid long waits for fill when L present. Both have tradeoffs (median increase / L slowdown).

Next steps / TODOs:
- Re-run with kernel-level tracing enabled (PR 1304 branch) to confirm kernel swap timings and NVTX markers.
- Try model variant with streaming disabled for L (send fewer incremental kernels) to see if tail persists.
- Capture full flamegraph + GPU timeline for a 60s window with repeated L starts to observe mem alloc/free.
- Evaluate enabling "batch isolation" where long-context requests are routed to a separate slot pool (cheap to test on staging).
- Write a short runbook describing recommended defaults: adaptive_timeout=8ms + priority lanes=on for latency-sensitive endpoints, with a note on fairness for long requests.

Loose notes / mental checklist:
- Is this 'tail amplification' just long-request induced queuing, or is there an additional kernel-prep cost (warm kernels)? Need kernel trace.
- Consider quick AB test on Dedicated pools: put L into dedicated GPU and keep S on shared — does it disappear?
- Watch out for false positives from client-side batching of S-gen (validated S-gen sends single requests).
- Keep in mind quantization: int8 memory patterns might make eviction more visible. Try fp16 run too.

Raw numbers snapshot (one 5-min window, mixed S200+L10):
- S: mean 48ms, median 22ms, p90 76ms, p95 131ms, p99 310ms (N=120k)
- L: mean 1.1s, median 980ms, p95 1.8s (N=6k)
- Batching: average batch size overall 3.6, but S observed 2.4 during L bursts

Notes-to-self: keep this file terse. If this reproduces on larger cluster, escalate to infra for scheduler-level policy. Share with Maya / Ibrahim once kernel traces in hand.

Random fragments (will remove in final note):
- observed ~0.5% of S requests hit >800ms in mixed heavy runs — customer-impacty.
- maybe add a fast-path single-request immediate dispatch queue (bypass waiting for batch fill) — prototype earlier existed but disabled (search PR history).

End of scratchpad.
